definition: The interdisciplinary field concerned with ensuring AI systems behave reliably, avoid unintended harmful behavior, and remain aligned with human values, especially as capabilities increase.
details: AI safety research spans technical work on alignment and robustness as well as broader questions about societal risks from increasingly capable AI systems, ranging from near-term harms to longer-term existential considerations.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is AI Safety.
